* Toronto stocks were expected to climb at the open on Wednesday as the market played catch up to New York after Tuesday's Canada Day holiday. * Gold was expecteded to weigh on market.
Toronto stocks were expected to rise at the open on Wednesday as the market played catch up to New York after Tuesday's Canada Day holiday.

"Yesterday the Dow rallied almost 50 points and we usually play catch up the day after if we've been out and the U.S. is still open, so that's positive. Plus our bonds and bills are enjoying solid rallies this morning," said MMS International technical analyst Katherine Beattie.
She said the gold sector would likely be a major weight on the index as gold prices continued to slide, but gains in other sectors should outpace losses by the precious metal.

London's official morning fix put the price of gold at its lowest level since March 24, 1993. Bullion opened today set at US$331.45 per ounce, down from an already teetering US$333.70 on Tuesday and perilously close to its next major support level at US$330.00.
Beattie said trading might be slightly cautious this morning ahead of the U.S. Federal Reserve rate announcement, but an unchanged policy was already priced into the market.
"Certainly the widespread belief is they're not going to raise rates. If (the Fed) were to raise rates, that would look for a huge sell-off this afternoon," Beattie said.
The Fed's policy-setting Federal Open Market Committee is expected to wind up its two-day meeting with a rate decision announcement at about 1415 EDT/1815 GMT.
While Canadian markets took a break for Canada Day on Tuesday, in New York the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 49.54 points to close at 7722.33 after a seesaw session.
Toronto's key stock index finished firmer on Monday, ending up 11.34 points at 6437.74.
--- STOCKS TO WATCH ---

* Crestar Energy Inc said early on Wednesday that it agreed to acquire Grad & Walker Energy Corp in a deal worth about C$336.2 million. Under the deal, Crestar would acquire Grad & Walker in exchange for C$13.50 in cash or 0.509 Crestar common share for each Grad & Walker common share.
